settings.description: Name players see for this server in the in-game browser and in query replies.
Longer text shown under the name in the server browser.
Optional web address for your community. The server browser turns it into a link players can click.
Players must enter this to connect. Leave it empty for an open server. The file keeps it in plain text.
Optional text, such as house rules, that a joining player has to confirm before the game lets them in. Leave it empty to skip that step.
Region tag the server browser sorts this server under.
The community's main language, spelled in English (German rather than Deutsch), so that searches in the server browser find it.
UDP port for game traffic. The game also uses the two ports right after it, so keep those free and open as well.
Listing mode: 0 not listed, 1 friends only (rarely useful on a dedicated host), 2 public in the browser.
Comma list of transports to switch off: LiteNetLib or SteamNetworking. Port-forwarded hosts usually drop the Steam relay.
Cap on how fast a new client downloads the world on first join. The engine tops out near 1300.
Lets console players find and join. Console listing also needs anti-cheat on, sanctions honoured and few slots.
Turns the anti-cheat on or off. Client-side code mods usually need it off; public servers usually keep it on.
When true, players under Epic Online Services sanctions may still join, which drops the server from crossplay lists.
Concurrent player slots. More slots cost memory and CPU, and crossplay servers must stay at 8 or fewer.
Part of the player cap set aside for players whose permission level qualifies. 0 means no slots are held back.
Permission level that unlocks the reserved slots. In this game a lower number is a higher rank.
Admins can still connect when the server is full, up to this many on top of the player cap.
Permission level that counts as admin for the full-server admin slots. Lower numbers rank higher.
PVP rule: 0 nobody, 1 allies only, 2 strangers only, 3 anyone may damage other players.
Party members closer than this many blocks to a kill get a share of its experience and count it for party kill quests.
When on, a returning player always gets the profile used on the previous visit; when off, any profile may be chosen at join.
Turns on the plain-text remote console the Dialwarden save and stop actions use.
TCP port of the remote console. It must not clash with the game ports or the dashboard port.
Console password. Empty keeps the console bound to loopback only; set one before exposing the port.
Number of bad console passwords one remote address may send before the console refuses that address for a while.
Length of the console ban, in seconds, for an address that sent too many bad passwords.
Windows only: a console window with live log output and a command line opens next to the server. Linux ignores it.
Keeps admin command use out of logs: 0 logs everything, 1 hides it from console and panel, 2 also from game clients, 3 everywhere.
File name of the admin, whitelist and ban file. It resolves inside the Saves folder of the data directory.
Path that moves saves and generated worlds. The demo sets it inside the server root; empty uses the user profile instead.
Turns on the built-in browser admin page. Logins come from the token list of the admin file.
HTTP port of the built-in dashboard. It must differ from the console port and the three game ports.
Needed only when players reach the dashboard through a reverse proxy or a domain: the complete address, with https and port. Empty means the server IP and dashboard port.
Renders explored map tiles to disk for the dashboard map view. Costs extra CPU and disk space.
World to load: RWG for a generated map, or a shipped one such as Navezgane, Pregen06k01 or Pregen08k01.
Starting text for the RWG generator; other GameWorld values ignore it. When a world from this seed and size already exists, the server loads it rather than generating a new one.
Map width and height in blocks for a generated RWG world, in steps of 2048 from 6144 to 10240. Crossplay servers are limited to 8192.
Name of the save, also used to place trees and other decoration. A new name means a new save; the RWG terrain layout does not change.
Game mode identifier; GameModeSurvival is the only value shipped for dedicated servers, so it is normally left alone.
Days of game time a chunk may go without visitors before it reverts to how it was generated. Land claims and bedrolls nearby protect it; -1 turns resets off.
Disk budget per save. Once reached, old chunks may be reset. Negative values remove the cap.
Cap on how much map each player can reveal, which bounds the size of the per-player map file.
Highest player level that still gets an enemy-free area on spawning, giving new characters a calm start.
Game-time hours that the new-player spawn protection stays in place.
Creative or cheat mode for everyone: free items and no build costs. Keep it off for survival play.
Zombies cannot spawn in a box around an active bedroll; this value is half its side length. Sleeper rooms touching that box stay empty once cleared.
Number of real days without a login by its owner after which a bedroll stops working.
Whether a first-time player may start next to a friend who is online: 0 never, 1 always, 2 only when that friend is in the forest biome.
Camera rule for all players: 0 free choice, 1 first person only, 2 third person only.
Permission level a streamer must hold to run the Twitch integration here; lower numbers rank higher.
Allows Twitch viewer actions during blood moons; the extra spawns can add noticeable server load.
How many land claim blocks each player may have placed in the world at the same time.
Width in blocks of the area a land claim block protects, measured with the claim block in the middle.
Players who are not friends cannot place claim blocks closer together than this many blocks.
Real-world days a player may stay offline before their claims stop protecting anything.
Protection curve for an absent owner's claim: 0 slow (linear), 1 fast (exponential), 2 none until the claim expires.
Factor by which claimed blocks get harder to break while their owner is logged in. 4 is the stock value; 0 means they take no damage.
Factor by which claimed blocks get harder to break while their owner is logged out. 4 is the stock value; 0 means they take no damage.
Minutes the online hardness factor keeps applying after the owner logs out; the offline factor takes over after that.
World-wide cap on live zombies; the game scales it up for hordes and sleepers. Large CPU impact.
Ceiling on animals alive at once across the map. Biomes still limit local spawns, so raise it only if many players spread far apart.
Largest view distance a client may request. Strong effect on server memory and CPU.
Upper bound on chunk mesh layers waiting to be built. A smaller queue uses less memory, but chunks may take longer to appear.
Turns on the dynamic mesh system, which shows player-modified areas correctly at a distance.
When on, only claimed areas get dynamic mesh updates; turning it off covers the whole world at a higher CPU cost.
Margin, counted in chunks, that dynamic mesh work extends past the edge of each land claim.
Dynamic mesh jobs the server works on at once. Raising it speeds processing and costs memory.

The console has no password, so it listens on loopback only; local hooks work, a remote Dialwarden cannot connect.
Without the console, the save and clean-stop actions fall back to a process signal.
The console or dashboard port overlaps the game ports (port, port+1, port+2) or each other.
A generated world (RWG) needs a seed; set one or choose a shipped map.
The anti-cheat is off on a publicly listed server.
Console crossplay needs the anti-cheat on, sanctions honoured, at most 8 players, public visibility and a world of 8192 or less.
SandboxCode is empty, so the server runs the default ruleset.
SandboxCode does not look valid: it should be a version letter followed by groups of three letters. Copy a fresh code from the game's Sandbox screen.
